reason: This passage from Genesis 27 depicts family dynamics within a patriarchal household rather than leaders acting antagonistically toward their people. Isaac blesses his sons (which is his patriarchal role), and Rebekah assists Jacob. While there is family conflict when Esau discovers Jacob received the blessing instead of him, this represents a dispute between siblings about inheritance, not antagonism from leaders toward the broader Hebrew people. The passage shows succession politics and familial preference rather than systemic opposition between leaders and their people.
